title: Writing to George Lewis and returning to New Orleans
summary: Zardis wrote to George Lewis from the country, was answered by George's wife, fell ill in 1965, and returned to the city.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: How was it that you, you wrote, I mean, I ever once, I got a letter, I mean a letter came to Preservation Hall, that you'd written, saying that you'd, you'd heard, you know, playing there. George, I wrote to George.

Oh, you wrote to George? Yeah, I wrote to George Lewis. See, George had went to Japan, and, well, I, I was in the country at that time, and I bought that place out there, and I wrote to George, I said, well, I got kind of tired, I said, out there. I said, well, I'm glad George. So, I wrote George a letter, and told him, I said, in case you need a bass player, let me know, I said, I'm willing to come back to town.

So, George didn't answer the letter, but Sandra answered the letter. She told me that she was glad to hear from me, and, well, she didn't know me, but she heard, you know, so much talk about it. So, I said, well, George is not here now, he's over in Japan, that's the time they left and went to Japan, see, see, but you'll be hearing more from us in the future, see. So, sure enough, I got a letter, quite two letters from Sandra, and she asked me when I were coming, so, I told her, I'll be most any time if I can, you know, get, you know, get a position, see, I said, well, all right, so, I stayed open that time around 65, well, I got sick over there, and, I went to a doctor out there in the library, so he said, I had to panic, he must rush me to the hospital here. I said, okay, so I had to go to the VA and get my papers, and after I got my papers, so, I got this 6 o'clock train that evening, I got here 11 o'clock at night, so, after I got off the bus, well, I rushed over to the VA hospital, when I got over there, they examined me, and they kept me over there, so, and I stayed there about, oh, about 28 days, and, uh, when I, when I got out, who I met but Cantrell, I said, Cantrell, I asked me where was I going, was I going back to the country? I said, yeah. They said, don't go back to the country, said, we need a man like you here, why don't you stay here? So, then he come and said, tell me about the job, you know, and everything, how it's good it is, so I said, well, I believe I will. So, and that's where, he asked me what I have to do to go back, I told him I had some cows and hoes and, you know, chickens, I said, well, I have to go back there and, you know, get rid of that stuff. So, he said, well, you go ahead back and write the man manure. So, which couple days after I went back, and I commenced selling all chickens, some of them I butchered and sold black market meat, you know, and sold chickens and different things like that. Now, the hardest trouble was me to get somebody to stay in the place out there. So, which I did, I got an old lady and an old man. I went about three, four places. I asked them if they wanted to stay, well, they didn't want to stay. So, it happened I went way around almost to St. Martinsville, and, uh, there's an old lady there, I know, I think so, and I asked them if they wanted to take you in my place. So, he told me, yes, do you want to stay, yes. So, you don't have nothing to pay but the electric and gas. So, I said, sure. So, they're still out there in the place now. So, that's when I came, came back here. Well, I came here one, one night, and I met Bill Russell. Bill had owed me $40 from that time. Really did. Bill said, Chester, I got some money for you. I said, oh, no. He said, yeah, I got some money for you. He said, I got $40. He said, I've been keeping that money for you all this time. I said, well, I only have interest on that money. And, uh, Bill gave me $40 right there at that gate there.
